Implemented the requested frontend/data-flow changes.

### Data and backend integration

Added two backend-supported frontend endpoints:

```text
GET /api/listings
GET /api/policy
```

`/api/listings` exposes database-backed catalog listings with:

- Total quantity
- Available quantity
- Checked-out quantity
- Category
- Location
- Equipment IDs

`/api/policy` exposes the configured standard loan duration to students without exposing admin-only settings.

The frontend API adapter now includes:

```javascript
mlmApi.listings()
mlmApi.policy()
```

No database schema changes were made.

### Equipment quantities

Student catalog quantities now come from `/api/listings`.

Admin equipment quantities now use the same database listing data, so both views display the same:

- Total quantity
- Available quantity
- Checked-out quantity

The admin page still uses individual equipment IDs for editing.

### Brand filters

Student and admin brand filters are now generated dynamically from backend-returned equipment/listing names.

There are no hardcoded Sony, Canon, Sigma, RØDE, or other brand filter options remaining in the catalog UI.

The database does not currently have a separate `brand` column. Brands are therefore derived from the database-provided listing/equipment names. A dedicated `brand` field would be needed if brand filtering must become fully authoritative.

### Extension requests

Added a functional extension request interface in the user booking history:

- Opens a proper extension dialog
- Shows booking and equipment details
- Allows selecting a new return date/time
- Requires a reason
- Submits through the existing extension endpoint
- Refreshes the booking history after submission

Admin requests now also display pending extension requests and provide:

- Approve extension
- Reject extension

These use the existing request-window API.

### Navigation and controls

Removed the catalog page’s redundant square notification and cart buttons.

For admins:

- The top navigation now labels the catalog link as `User View`.
- This makes it clear that it switches to the student-facing interface.
- Admin navigation remains available through the top bar.

Added a `Log out` button for authenticated users and admins. It calls the existing logout endpoint and redirects to the login page.

### Removed dashboard page

Removed:

```text
Media Lab Front/pages/admin/dashboard.html
Media Lab Front/js/admin-dashboard.js
```

All dashboard references were removed. The admin interface now starts from the equipment management page.

### Static information reduced

Removed static catalog brand lists and static notification counts.

Booking loan-duration text now comes from the backend policy endpoint.

Equipment/request quantities and request extension data are loaded from backend responses.

Some UI labels remain static because they describe actions or sections rather than application data.

##1. Overall objective
The goal is to bring the new Figma design into the actual application without losing existing features or breaking the backend integration.

A. The separate Figma frontend prototype
- This is the visual/design reference.

B. The latest Git repository
- This contains the actual application and its existing functionality.
- Its current frontend is the source of truth for existing user workflows, UI behavior, routes, and frontend interactions.
- Its backend, database, API adapter, and related server code are the source of truth for data structures, endpoint contracts, authentication, authorization, and persistence.
- Preserve and adapt these existing systems rather than replacing them with the prototype's mock implementation.

The final result should look like the Figma prototype, but behave like the real Media Lab Manager application.

##2. Inspect the project before changing anything

1. The actual frontend folder in the repository, especially its HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files.
2. The separate Figma prototype folder and all of its relevant HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and assets.
3. The backend/server folder, including routes, middleware, authentication, and request/response formats.
4. The database schema, database commands, seed data, and any documentation that explains the data model.

7. Any README or setup instructions relevant to running the app.

Compare the prototype with the actual frontend and produce a short plan before making changes. Identify:
- Which pages and visual components need to be redesigned.
- Which existing frontend features and workflows each page currently supports.
- Which prototype features are only visual or mock implementations.
- Which existing API endpoints and database fields each workflow depends on.
- Any differences or conflicts between the prototype and actual application.

Do not make assumptions about the backend or database. Inspect the actual code and use its real endpoint names, data fields, status values, and validation requirements.

##3. Scope and file organization

Make the design and integration changes in the actual frontend folder in the Git repository.

Keep the existing multi-page structure:
- Multiple HTML files are allowed and should remain separate where that is how the actual application is organized.
- Keep CSS in separate stylesheet files.
- Keep JavaScript in separate files.
- Preserve the existing folder and file organization where practical.
- Reuse shared CSS for common design elements instead of duplicating styles across pages.

Do not convert the application into one giant HTML file.

Do not replace the actual frontend folder with the Figma prototype folder. The prototype is a reference to adapt from, not a replacement for the actual application.

Do not delete the separate Figma prototype. Keep it available for comparison and reference.

Do not modify backend or database files just to make the new design easier to implement. If a backend change appears necessary, explain why and identify the exact requirement before changing it. Prefer adapting the frontend to the existing backend contract.

Do not commit or push any changes. I will review the result and handle Git operations separately.

## 4. Design requirements: match the Figma prototype

Preserve the prototype's visual identity and design decisions, including:
- Page layout and hierarchy
- Navigation style and placement
- Header and sidebar treatment, if present
- Typography and text hierarchy
- Colors, backgrounds, borders, shadows, and corner radii
- Spacing, alignment, sizing, and responsive layout
- Buttons, links, form controls, cards, tables, status labels, and modal/dialog styles
- Icons and other visual assets
- Loading, empty, error, success, and disabled states where shown or needed

Use the Figma prototype's design as the reference for appearance, but use the actual application’s labels, data, and workflows.

Do not make an unrelated redesign or introduce a different visual style.

Where the prototype has a component or page that is not present in the actual app, determine whether it corresponds to an existing application feature before adding it. Do not invent new product functionality without a clear basis in the existing app or design.

If the Figma design is incomplete for a particular page or state, follow the established design language from the prototype and retain the existing page's behavior and content.

## 5. Preserve existing application functionality

The redesigned frontend must retain all functionality that currently exists in the actual frontend and is supported by the backend.

Inspect the actual code to identify all existing features, event handlers, form validations, API calls, state changes, and navigation paths. Do not rely only on this checklist.

At minimum, examine and preserve the relevant workflows for:

### User workflows
- Login and session handling
- User identity and account information
- Equipment catalog
- Equipment availability and status
- Search, filtering, sorting, and equipment details
- Booking/request creation
- Request submission validation and confirmation
- Viewing active bookings and request history
- Pickup passes and pickup workflow
- Return workflow and recording return condition
- Damage reporting
- Extension requests
- Notifications
- User navigation and sign-out

### Admin workflows
- Admin authentication and authorization
- Dashboard and statistics
- Equipment management
- Request review
- Approving and rejecting requests
- Cancellation, if supported
- Pickup and return administration, if supported
- Damage and extension review, if supported
- Audit history
- Outbox or other admin views, if supported by the current application

This list is a guide. The actual repository determines which of these workflows exist and what each one does.

Do not remove a working feature simply because the Figma prototype does not show it. Find a suitable place for it in the new design while keeping its behavior intact.

Do not add decorative controls that appear functional but do nothing. Every visible interactive element should either perform its intended action or be clearly presented as disabled/unavailable.

## 6. Adapt the prototype's mock data to the real application

The Figma prototype may use fixed or hardcoded data, such as a particular camera, equipment list, availability status, user, or booking.

Replace those fixed values with real data from the existing application API/database wherever the feature is data-driven.

Examples:
- Equipment cards should be populated from the actual equipment endpoint and use the real equipment fields.
- Equipment IDs must use the real ID format and values returned by the backend.
- Availability and status labels must reflect the actual backend data and status definitions.
- Booking forms must submit the fields expected by the real backend.
- Request history should load the signed-in user's real requests.
- Admin tables and dashboards should use actual backend responses.
- Do not assume a specific camera or equipment item always exists.
- Do not hardcode availability, booking records, user details, or request statuses that should come from the database.

For each prototype element with sample data, determine whether it is:
1. Static presentation content that belongs in the UI,
2. A placeholder that must be replaced with backend data, or
3. A mock-only behavior that must be replaced with the actual application workflow.

If the prototype has sample equipment or sample bookings that are not in the database, do not create fake records in the real database just to make the design appear populated.

## 7. Preserve and adapt the actual API integration

The existing frontend and backend already have an API contract. Inspect it and keep the new frontend compatible with it.

- Reuse the existing API adapter where possible.
- Preserve endpoint paths, HTTP methods, request bodies, response field names, and error handling unless the actual backend code proves a change is required.
- Update page JavaScript to work with the actual API adapter and real data structures.
- Keep API configuration centralized and configurable for local development.
- Do not scatter hardcoded API URLs across page scripts.
- Do not silently substitute prototype mock data when a real API request fails.
- Handle loading, empty, and error states in a user-friendly way.
- Avoid unnecessary duplicate API calls.
- Keep user and admin data access consistent with the existing backend authorization rules.

If the prototype uses a different API structure, do not blindly copy it. Adapt its interface components and interactions to the existing repository's API contract.

If an endpoint is missing or a workflow cannot be supported by the current backend, document the exact missing endpoint or data requirement. Do not invent an endpoint and pretend it exists.

## 8. Authentication, sessions, and protected pages

Preserve the current authentication and session architecture from the actual application and backend.

- Inspect the current login implementation and the server's authentication behavior.
- Keep the actual login provider and authentication flow that the repository currently uses.
- Do not replace real authentication with the prototype's mock login.
- Do not bypass session checks or redirect logic just to make the new pages easier to preview.
- Do not remove admin authorization checks or allow a regular user to access admin operations.
- Keep protected routes protected.
- Make sure the redesigned login page connects to the existing authentication flow.
- Ensure a successful login leads to the appropriate existing application page.
- Ensure session expiry, unauthenticated access, and sign-out still work as intended.
- Do not place secrets, API keys, passwords, OAuth client secrets, or tokens in frontend source code.

If a local prototype mode exists in the Figma prototype, do not transfer its authentication bypass into the actual app. It may be retained only in the separate prototype folder, not in the actual application.

## 9. Preserve data integrity and application rules

Keep all existing validation and business rules.

Examples include:
- Required form fields
- Valid equipment identifiers
- Valid pickup and return dates/times
- Availability checks and prevention of invalid or duplicate requests
- Existing request status transitions
- Role-based permissions
- Return condition and damage handling
- Extension rules and approval requirements
- Any backend-side validation and error messages

Do not implement important business rules only in the browser if the backend already enforces them.

Do not bypass server validation because a prototype interaction is simpler.

When a backend operation succeeds, update the UI using the actual response or reload the relevant data as appropriate. When it fails, show a meaningful error and keep the UI consistent with the server's actual state.

## 10. JavaScript and page integration

Update the actual frontend's JavaScript as needed to connect the new design to existing application behavior.

- Preserve existing event handlers and business logic.
- Adjust DOM selectors and element IDs/classes where the new markup differs.
- Ensure each page's JavaScript is loaded in the correct order and only where needed.
- Keep shared logic in shared scripts such as the existing API/session modules.
- Avoid duplicating authentication, API, or workflow logic across pages.
- Ensure forms still validate and submit correctly.
- Ensure navigation links point to the actual application pages.
- Ensure dynamic UI components render correctly with backend data.
- Avoid hardcoded prototype-only element references that do not exist in the actual page.
- Keep code readable and maintainable, with comments where integration decisions are non-obvious.

If a design component needs new JavaScript behavior, implement it in the appropriate existing or new JS file. Do not put application logic into inline event attributes in the HTML.

## 11. Responsive behavior and accessibility

Preserve the Figma design at desktop sizes and adapt it for smaller screens.

Check:
- Navigation behavior on mobile and tablet
- Cards, tables, forms, and dialogs at narrow widths
- Text wrapping and overflow
- Keyboard navigation
- Visible focus states
- Labels for form inputs
- Appropriate button/link semantics
- Accessible names for icon-only controls
- Contrast and legibility

Do not sacrifice usability to reproduce a screenshot at only one fixed screen size.

## 12. Implementation workflow

Follow this sequence:

PHASE A — Inspect and plan
1. Locate the actual frontend, Figma prototype, backend/server, and database folders.
2. Inspect the relevant source files and Figma design.
3. Compare the current pages and prototype pages.
4. Map each existing feature to the page/component that will receive the new design.
5. Map each data-driven component to its actual API endpoint and data fields.
6. Identify any conflicts, missing endpoints, or uncertainties.
7. Present a concise plan before editing.

PHASE B — Implement the design
1. Update the actual frontend HTML markup to reflect the Figma design.
2. Update or create CSS files to match the design system.
3. Update the actual frontend JavaScript to work with the revised markup.
4. Connect all data-driven components to the existing API adapter.
5. Preserve authentication, authorization, and session handling.
6. Replace prototype fixed data with backend data where appropriate.
7. Keep all changes within the actual frontend folder unless a backend change has been explicitly justified and approved.

PHASE C — Validate
1. Check every changed JavaScript file for syntax errors.
2. Check all HTML references to CSS, JS, and assets.
3. Check that every referenced file exists.
4. Check that navigation between pages works.
5. Check that direct access to protected pages still follows the actual authentication/session rules.
6. Check that the redesigned login page works with the existing authentication implementation.
7. Check the browser console and network requests for errors.
8. Test each important workflow with the actual backend if it is available.
9. Test empty, loading, success, and failure states where practical.
10. Confirm that no existing application feature was unintentionally removed.
11. Confirm that no backend/database file was changed unless that was necessary and approved.

Do not claim a feature works unless it has been tested. If you cannot run the application or backend, report that limitation and give me the exact manual test steps needed.

## 13. Git safety
- Do not commit or push changes.
- Do not switch branches or reset the repository.
- Do not discard existing uncommitted work.
- Before editing, inspect `git status` and note any pre-existing changes.
- Do not overwrite files with existing user or teammate modifications without examining their contents.
- At the end, summarize the files you changed so I can review them before staging.

## 14. Final report

1. **Design changes**

   - Which Figma design elements were applied.

2. **Functionality preserved**

3. **Backend and database integration**

content.text:
Implemented the requested frontend updates in the latest `Media-Lab_Manager` repository.

### Changes made

- Restricted profile booking history:
  - Only administrators can select and view another user’s bookings.
  - Students, faculty, staff, and other non-admin users are always limited to their own history.
  - Query-string `userId` values are ignored for non-admin users.

- Fixed My History tabs:
  - Current Bookings, Past Bookings, and Pending Requests now visibly update their selected state.
  - The page now opens on Current Bookings.
  - Active tab state persists after extension requests refresh the list.

- Updated action labels:
  - Replaced “View Details” with “Return & Damage”.
  - Added navigation context so the return form knows where it was opened from.

- Fixed Return & Damage cancellation:
  - Cancel from the history page returns to `history.html`.

Changes required:
work on the git repository (Media-Lab_Manager)
1. The request Extension UI is (cluttered and 50 % un-appealing) unmatched with the rest of the UI. Make a more readable interface and makes sure it matches the whole style
2. On clicking the buttons in damage report, the highlight doesn't change according to the button press. Make sure the button highlight matches the button click so it is not confusing
3. If there are multiple equipment, the damage report shows it twice for all of the equipment. The damage report even if there are multiple equipment in a single booking, make sure that each equipment in a booking gets a separate damage report.
4. I can fill the damage report under current bookings, and it goes to the past bookings as intended. But, the damage report option is also available there, so I can fill multiple damage forms. Make sure that a user can only fill one damage report per equipment.

6. For equipment catalog, each equipment catalog card feels cluttered, especially the gap between equipment name and equipment image is very small. Increase that gap to a reasonable amount so it's no longer cluttered. 
7. The settings page for Admin is still inconsistent and feels disconnected from the rest of the navigation functions (requests , equipments, damage report)
8. Change the name of the navigation function named Profile under the Admin's user view. It currently allows the admin to see the booking history of each admin. So change the name to User History. Make sure this change is only visible to the Admin and it doesn't affect the user's profile function in their navigation bar. Also the dropdown button for selecting a specific user in this tab (to see other user's booking history for admin) is bit too close with the text on the left side of it. Make sure there is a reasonable gap between them. 

If any of the above bugs/ changes are not fixable give reasons as to why it is not possible.

        raise ApiError("endsAt must be after startsAt")
    requested = db.connection.execute(
        "SELECT starts_at FROM time_windows WHERE request_id=? AND kind='pickup' AND status='requested' ORDER BY id LIMIT 1",
        (request_id,),
    ).fetchone()
    if requested is None:
        raise ApiError("Original pickup slot not found", 409)
    requested_start = iso_date(requested["starts_at"], "requested pickup start")
    earliest = requested_start - timedelta(hours=24)
    latest = requested_start - timedelta(minutes=20)
    if starts < earliest or starts > latest:
        raise ApiError("Pickup slot must start between 24 hours and 20 minutes before the requested pickup time")

def request_view(request_id: int):
    """Return one request with its items, windows, and return submission."""
    request = db._request_view(request_id)
    if request:
        request["return_submission"] = return_submission_view(request_id)
    return request


def return_submission_view(request_id: int):
    """Return the student submission and staff verification details."""
    row = db.connection.execute(
        "SELECT * FROM return_submissions WHERE request_id=?", (request_id,)
    ).fetchone()
    if not row:
        return None
    result = dict(row)
    for field in ("photo_references", "verification_photos"):
        try:
            result[field] = json.loads(result[field] or "[]")
        except (TypeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            result[field] = []
    return result


def return_payload(data: dict, request_id: int, user_id: int):
    """Normalize return-submission fields and attach the authenticated user."""
    claimed = data.get("claimedReturnedAt") or data.get("returnedAt")
    iso_date(claimed, "claimedReturnedAt")
    photos = data.get("photoReferences", data.get("photos", []))
    if not isinstance(photos, list):
        raise ApiError("photoReferences must be a list")
    return {
        "requestId": request_id,
        "submittedBy": user_id,
        "claimedReturnedAt": claimed,
        "studentCondition": data.get("studentCondition", data.get("condition", "")),
        "damageDescription": data.get("damageDescription", data.get("notes", "")),
        "missingItems": data.get("missingItems", ""),
        "photoReferences": photos,
    }


def create_return_submission(data: dict):
    """Store or replace a student's pending return submission."""
    existing = db.connection.execute(
        "SELECT verification_status FROM return_submissions WHERE request_id=?", (data["requestId"],)
    ).fetchone()
    if existing and existing["verification_status"] in {"verified_returned", "verified_damaged", "missing_items"}:
        raise ApiError("This return has already been verified", 409)
    db.connection.execute(
        """INSERT INTO return_submissions
           (request_id,submitted_by,claimed_returned_at,student_condition,damage_description,missing_items,photo_references,verification_status)
           VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,'return_submitted')
           ON CONFLICT(request_id) DO UPDATE SET
             submitted_by=excluded.submitted_by,submitted_at=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
             claimed_returned_at=excluded.claimed_returned_at,student_condition=excluded.student_condition,
             damage_description=excluded.damage_description,missing_items=excluded.missing_items,
             photo_references=excluded.photo_references,verification_status='return_submitted',
             verified_at=NULL,verified_by=NULL,actual_returned_at=NULL,staff_condition='',staff_notes='',verification_photos='[]'""",
        (data["requestId"], data["submittedBy"], data["claimedReturnedAt"], data["studentCondition"],
         data["damageDescription"], data["missingItems"], json.dumps(data["photoReferences"])),
    )
    db._audit(data["submittedBy"], "request", data["requestId"], "return_submitted", data)
    db._emit("return.submitted", "request", data["requestId"], data)
    db.connection.commit()
    return return_submission_view(data["requestId"])


def verify_return_submission(data: dict):

    def check_availability(self, equipment_ids: int | list[int], starts_at: str, ends_at: str) -> list[int]:
        ids = equipment_ids if isinstance(equipment_ids, list) else [equipment_ids]
        if not ids:
            return []
        marks = ",".join("?" for _ in ids)
        query = f"""SELECT DISTINCT ri.equipment_id FROM request_items ri
          JOIN requests r ON r.id=ri.request_id JOIN time_windows w ON w.request_id=r.id
          WHERE ri.equipment_id IN ({marks})
            AND r.status IN ('pending','approved','pickup_pending','picked_up','overdue')
            AND w.status IN ('requested','approved') AND w.starts_at < ? AND w.ends_at > ?"""
        return [row["equipment_id"] for row in self.connection.execute(query, [*ids, starts_at, ends_at])]

    def _request_view(self, request_id: int) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        row = self.connection.execute(

            "FROM requests r JOIN users u ON u.id=r.requester_id WHERE r.id=?", (request_id,)
        ).fetchone()
        result = _row(row)
        if result is None:
            return None
        result["items"] = _rows(self.connection.execute(
            "SELECT ri.*,e.asset_code,e.name,e.status AS equipment_status FROM request_items ri "
            "JOIN equipment e ON e.id=ri.equipment_id WHERE ri.request_id=?", (request_id,)
        ))
        result["windows"] = _rows(self.connection.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM time_windows WHERE request_id=? ORDER BY starts_at", (request_id,)
        ))
        return result

def request_view(request_id: int):
    """Return one request with its items, windows, and return submission."""
    request = db._request_view(request_id)
    if request:
        request["return_submission"] = return_submission_view(request_id)
    return request


def return_submission_view(request_id: int):
    """Return the student submission and staff verification details."""
    row = db.connection.execute(
        "SELECT * FROM return_submissions WHERE request_id=?", (request_id,)
    ).fetchone()
    if not row:
        return None
    result = dict(row)
    for field in ("photo_references", "verification_photos"):
        try:
            result[field] = json.loads(result[field] or "[]")
        except (TypeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            result[field] = []
    return result


def return_payload(data: dict, request_id: int, user_id: int):
    """Normalize return-submission fields and attach the authenticated user."""
    claimed = data.get("claimedReturnedAt") or data.get("returnedAt")
    iso_date(claimed, "claimedReturnedAt")
    photos = data.get("photoReferences", data.get("photos", []))
    if not isinstance(photos, list):
        raise ApiError("photoReferences must be a list")
    return {
        "requestId": request_id,
        "submittedBy": user_id,
        "claimedReturnedAt": claimed,
        "studentCondition": data.get("studentCondition", data.get("condition", "")),
        "damageDescription": data.get("damageDescription", data.get("notes", "")),
        "missingItems": data.get("missingItems", ""),
        "photoReferences": photos,
    }


def create_return_submission(data: dict):
    """Store or replace a student's pending return submission."""
    existing = db.connection.execute(
        "SELECT verification_status FROM return_submissions WHERE request_id=?", (data["requestId"],)
    ).fetchone()
    if existing and existing["verification_status"] in {"verified_returned", "verified_damaged", "missing_items"}:
        raise ApiError("This return has already been verified", 409)
    db.connection.execute(
        """INSERT INTO return_submissions
           (request_id,submitted_by,claimed_returned_at,student_condition,damage_description,missing_items,photo_references,verification_status)
           VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,'return_submitted')
           ON CONFLICT(request_id) DO UPDATE SET
             submitted_by=excluded.submitted_by,submitted_at=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
             claimed_returned_at=excluded.claimed_returned_at,student_condition=excluded.student_condition,
             damage_description=excluded.damage_description,missing_items=excluded.missing_items,
             photo_references=excluded.photo_references,verification_status='return_submitted',
             verified_at=NULL,verified_by=NULL,actual_returned_at=NULL,staff_condition='',staff_notes='',verification_photos='[]'""",
        (data["requestId"], data["submittedBy"], data["claimedReturnedAt"], data["studentCondition"],
         data["damageDescription"], data["missingItems"], json.dumps(data["photoReferences"])),
    )
    db._audit(data["submittedBy"], "request", data["requestId"], "return_submitted", data)
    db._emit("return.submitted", "request", data["requestId"], data)
    db.connection.commit()
    return return_submission_view(data["requestId"])

    def check_availability(self, equipment_ids: int | list[int], starts_at: str, ends_at: str) -> list[int]:
        ids = equipment_ids if isinstance(equipment_ids, list) else [equipment_ids]
        if not ids:
            return []
        marks = ",".join("?" for _ in ids)
        query = f"""SELECT DISTINCT ri.equipment_id FROM request_items ri
          JOIN requests r ON r.id=ri.request_id JOIN time_windows w ON w.request_id=r.id
          WHERE ri.equipment_id IN ({marks})
            AND r.status IN ('pending','approved','pickup_pending','picked_up','overdue')
            AND w.status IN ('requested','approved') AND w.starts_at < ? AND w.ends_at > ?"""
        return [row["equipment_id"] for row in self.connection.execute(query, [*ids, starts_at, ends_at])]

    def _request_view(self, request_id: int) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        row = self.connection.execute(
            "SELECT r.*,u.krea_id,u.name AS requester_name,u.email AS requester_email "
            "FROM requests r JOIN users u ON u.id=r.requester_id WHERE r.id=?", (request_id,)
        ).fetchone()
        result = _row(row)
        if result is None:
            return None
        result["items"] = _rows(self.connection.execute(
            "SELECT ri.*,e.asset_code,e.name,e.status AS equipment_status FROM request_items ri "
            "JOIN equipment e ON e.id=ri.equipment_id WHERE ri.request_id=?", (request_id,)
        ))
        result["windows"] = _rows(self.connection.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM time_windows WHERE request_id=? ORDER BY starts_at", (request_id,)
        ))
        return result

    def create_request(self, data: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        ids = [item.get("id", item) if isinstance(item, dict) else item for item in data.get("equipmentIds", data.get("items", []))]
        if not data.get("requesterId") or not ids:
            raise ValueError("requesterId and equipmentIds are required")
        with self._transaction():
            user = self.connection.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id=?", (data["requesterId"],)).fetchone()
            if user is None:
                raise ValueError("user not found")
            if user["banned"]:
                raise ValueError("user is banned")
            marks = ",".join("?" for _ in ids)
            equipment_rows = self.connection.execute(f"SELECT id,status FROM equipment WHERE id IN ({marks})", ids).fetchall()
            found_ids = {row["id"] for row in equipment_rows}
            missing_ids = [equipment_id for equipment_id in ids if equipment_id not in found_ids]
            if missing_ids:
                raise ValueError("equipment not found: " + ",".join(map(str, missing_ids)))
            unavailable = [row["id"] for row in equipment_rows if row["status"] != "available"]
            if unavailable:
                raise ValueError("equipment unavailable: " + ",".join(map(str, unavailable)))
            conflicts = self.check_availability(ids, data.get("pickupStartsAt"), data.get("returnEndsAt"))
            if conflicts:
                raise ValueError("equipment unavailable: " + ",".join(map(str, conflicts)))
            cur = self.connection.execute(
                "INSERT INTO requests(requester_id,purpose,academic_priority) VALUES (?,?,?)",
                (data["requesterId"], data.get("purpose", ""), data.get("academicPriority", 0)),
            )
            request_id = cur.lastrowid
            for equipment_id in ids:
                self.connection.execute("INSERT INTO request_items(request_id,equipment_id) VALUES (?,?)", (request_id, equipment_id))
                self.connection.execute("UPDATE equipment SET status='requested',updated_at=? WHERE id=?", (_now(), equipment_id))
            for kind, start_key, end_key in (("pickup", "pickupStartsAt", "pickupEndsAt"), ("return", "returnStartsAt", "returnEndsAt")):
                if data.get(start_key) and data.get(end_key):
                    self.connection.execute("INSERT INTO time_windows(request_id,kind,starts_at,ends_at) VALUES (?,?,?,?)",
                                            (request_id, kind, data[start_key], data[end_key]))
            self._audit(data["requesterId"], "request", request_id, "created", {"equipmentIds": ids})
            self._emit("request.created", "request", request_id, {"equipmentIds": ids})
        return self._request_view(request_id)

    def set_request_status(self, request_id: int, status: str, actor_id: int | None = None, details: dict[str, Any] | None = None):
        details = details or {}
        with self._transaction():
            request = self.connection.execute("SELECT * FROM requests WHERE id=?", (request_id,)).fetchone()
            if request is None:
                raise ValueError("request not found")
            self.connection.execute(
                "UPDATE requests SET status=?,rejection_reason=?,approval_notes=?,updated_at=? WHERE id=?",
                (status, details.get("reason", request["rejection_reason"]), details.get("notes", request["approval_notes"]), _now(), request_id),
            )
            self.connection.execute("UPDATE request_items SET status=? WHERE request_id=?", (status, request_id))
            if status in ("approved", "pickup_pending"):
                self.connection.execute("UPDATE equipment SET status='pickup_pending',updated_at=? WHERE id IN (SELECT equipment_id FROM request_items WHERE request_id=?)", (_now(), request_id))
            elif status in ("rejected", "cancelled"):
                self.connection.execute("UPDATE equipment SET status='available',updated_at=? WHERE id IN (SELECT equipment_id FROM request_items WHERE request_id=?)", (_now(), request_id))
            self._audit(actor_id, "request", request_id, status, details)
            self._emit(f"request.{status}", "request", request_id, details)
        return self._request_view(request_id)

content.text:
Implemented the frontend changes in the latest `Media-Lab_Manager` repository.

### Completed changes

- Redesigned the extension request modal:
  - Improved spacing, typography, fields, buttons, and overlay styling.
  - Matches the rest of the application’s card and form design.

- Fixed damage-condition highlighting:
  - Each selected condition now receives the active teal highlight.
  - Works independently for every equipment item.

- Added per-equipment return sections:
  - A booking with multiple equipment now displays a separate condition and notes section for each item.
  - Equipment names and request-item IDs come from the backend response.

- Prevented repeated return submissions:
  - Return links are hidden after a booking already has a `return_submission`.
  - Direct access to the return page also shows that the report was already submitted.

- Updated severity filtering:
  - Admin severity filter options are now generated from the actual severity values returned by the backend.
  - No longer assumes fixed frontend values such as `minor`, `major`, or `critical`.

- Improved catalog card spacing:
  - Increased spacing between equipment imagery, metadata, and equipment names.

- Improved admin settings consistency:
  - Settings page now uses the same content width, spacing, card sizing, and responsive grid as other admin pages.

- Renamed admin profile navigation:
  - Administrators now see `User History`.
  - Regular users still see `Profile`.
  - Added better spacing between the admin user selector label and dropdown.

### Backend limitation discovered

The backend currently stores student return submissions at the booking level through:

`POST /api/requests/{id}/return`

The backend’s separate item-level damage endpoint is:

`POST /api/request-items/{id}/damage`

However, that endpoint is restricted to staff users. Therefore:

- The frontend now collects separate condition reports for each equipment item.
- These are stored inside the existing booking-level return submission fields as structured JSON.
- True independent database rows for each student-submitted equipment damage report require a backend/API change.

Additionally, the backend currently creates damage reports with severity `"reported"` when staff records a damaged return. The frontend cannot change that database behavior without modifying the backend.

### Files changed

- `Media Lab Front/css/admin.css`
- `Media Lab Front/css/catalog.css`
- `Media Lab Front/css/history.css`
- `Media Lab Front/css/return.css`
- `Media Lab Front/js/admin-history.js`
- `Media Lab Front/js/history.js`
- `Media Lab Front/js/nav.js`
- `Media Lab Front/js/profile.js`
- `Media Lab Front/js/return.js`

No backend or database files were changed.

Validation completed:

- All JavaScript files passed `node --check`.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Browser/API integration testing was not run in this environment.

- Approved
- Pickup pending
- Picked up
- Overdue

- Increased spacing from the image border
- A separate white content area
- Improved line height and visual separation
- No text overlay on the equipment image

content.text:
Implemented the frontend fixes and investigated the missing damage reports.

### 1. Return & Damage form UI

The form now has a clearer layout:

- Separate card for each equipment item
- Clearly visible condition buttons
- 2×2 condition grid on desktop
- Strong selected-state styling with radio indicators
- Improved spacing, borders, descriptions, and notes fields
- Better mobile layout
- Consistent Media Lab colors, cards, and buttons

### 2. Why reports were missing from the admin console

The student submission uses:

`POST /api/requests/{id}/return`

The backend stores this in `return_submissions`, not in the `damage_reports` table.

The separate item-level damage endpoint:

`POST /api/request-items/{id}/damage`

is staff-only, so the frontend cannot call it as a student without violating backend authorization.

### Fix applied

The admin Damage Reports page now loads:

- Existing database damage reports
- Student return submissions containing per-equipment damage information

Student submissions are displayed as pending/open damage reports in the admin interface, including:

- Equipment
- Borrower
- Severity
- Description
- Submission date
- Return condition

No backend or database files were changed.

### Validation

- All JavaScript files passed `node --check`.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Browser/API testing was not run in this environment.

content.text:
Updated the return/damage form structure and investigated the missing admin reports.

### Return & Damage form

The page now uses a full-width layout closer to your reference image:

- Single full-width return checklist card
- Request and equipment summary across the top
- Separate per-equipment condition sections
- Clear Excellent / Good / Minor Damage / Major Damage buttons
- Larger notes areas
- Photo upload retained
- Better spacing and responsive behavior
- Existing submission and duplicate-prevention logic preserved

### Why the damage report was not appearing

The student form submits to:

`POST /api/requests/{id}/return`

The backend stores this as a `return_submission`, not as a row in `damage_reports`.

The admin page previously loaded only:

`GET /api/damage-reports`

Therefore, student-submitted damage details were not shown.

The admin frontend now combines:

- Existing database damage reports
- Damage details embedded in student return submissions

These student submissions are displayed as open/pending reports in the Damage Reports tab, using the real request, equipment, borrower, severity, and submission data.

No backend or database files were changed.

- `git diff --check` passed.
- Browser/API testing was not run in this environment.
